title: Red spider mite on Brinjal - Sri Lanka

Header: Red spider mite on Brinjal - Sri Lanka
Tetranychus spp. In Sinhala - “Rathu makulu maitawa”; In Tamil –“Sivappu silanthi sittunni”

Prevention: Destruction of residues of previous crop.
Maha to avoid high temperatures that favour mites.
Establish vigorous plants by using recommended fertilizer rates with organic manure.
Crop rotation with maize or pulses.
Monitoring: Usually mite infestation takes place after one month of planting.
Observe lower surface of leaves with a hand lens for mites and their webs.
Look for white/yellow dots on upper surface of leaves or complete yellowing of leaves.
Look for sooty mould development on upper surface of lower leaves.
Apply chemical controls where there is an average of more than 7 mites per leaf.
Conserve natural enemies (predatory mites, lady bird beetles, lace wings, etc.)
Direct Control: Spray water to reduce mite population.
Neem seed water extract at the rate of 400g/10l.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
Do not apply sulphur when temperature is higher than 32°C; WHO class
U (Unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use); Mites growth regulator.
